title: Interior degree bounds transferred to the degree-18 interface
author: Main
setting: Pure claims: A is any simple K4/I5-free graph on 18 vertices, a=e(A)=85-q, 0<=q<=35. Ambient claims additionally assume a K5/I5-free graph G on 43 vertices, a degree-18 root v, A=N(v), B=M(v), epsilon_u=d_G(u)-18 in [0,6], E=sum_A epsilon_u, r_u=|N_B(u)|=17+epsilon_u-d_A(u). A is not assumed I4-free.
external_premises: README.md State of the Art: published maxima E(4,4,n)=45,50,55,60,68 for n=13,14,15,16,17, respectively (McKay-Radziszowski 1992 as recorded).
README.md State of the Art: 41<=e(4,5,17)<=79 (Angeltveit-McKay, arXiv:2409.15709v2 Appendix A Table 1 as recorded).

R(3,4)=9 and R(3,5)=14 as recorded in README.md State of the Art; R(4,5)=25 as recorded in docs/mathematical_baseline.md; Mantel's theorem (classical). External literature/censuses not recertified here.

claims.scope: Every pure A in the setting, every u in A; no connectivity, E, or x hypothesis.
claims.conclusion: Every vertex has d_A(u)>=L(q), where L(q)=6,5,4 at q=0,1,2; 4 for q=3..5; 3 for q=6..10; 2 for q=11..15; 1 for q=16; 0 for q=17..35. Equivalently: L=0 for a<=68, 1 at a=69, 2 at a=70..74, 3 at a=75..79, 4 at a=80..83, 5 at a=84, 6 at a=85. If A is connected replace L by max(1,L).
proof: Fix u and put s=d_A(u), S=N_A(u), H=A-({u} union S). The induced H is K4/I4-free: an I4 in H with u would form I5 in A. Only H, not all of A, is I4-free.
The induced S is triangle-free, since a triangle with u gives K4. Hence e(S)<=floor(s^2/4) by Mantel.
For each z in S, N_H(z) is triangle-free (a triangle with z would form K4) and I4-free (as a subset of H). Therefore |N_H(z)|<=8 by R(3,4)=9, so e(S,H)<=8s.

For s=0,1,2,3,4 the recorded maximum U(17-s) applies to H, and the exact edge partition gives a=s+e(S)+e(S,H)+e(H)<=U(17-s)+9s+floor(s^2/4). These caps are respectively 68,69,74,79,85. Thus a>68 forces s>=1, a>69 forces s>=2, a>74 forces s>=3, a>79 forces s>=4.

Independently A-u is (4,5)-free on 17 vertices, giving a-s<=79 and s>=a-79. Taking the maximum of these integral lower bounds and zero proves the table. Connectivity adds s>=1 since A has more than one vertex.
claims.improvement: The old max(0,6-q) floor is strictly strengthened for every q=3..16. In particular a=82 now forces minimum degree4 rather than3; a=80 forces4 rather than1; a=75 forces3 rather than0. No isolated-graph existence is asserted at any parameter.

claims.scope: Every pure A above, every vertex u.
claims.conclusion: d_A(u)<=D(q)=min(13,44-q). Thus at q=32,33,34,35 the interior maximum degree is at most12,11,10,9, respectively.
proof: A-u remains (4,5)-free on 17 vertices and has at least41 edges, so a-d_A(u)>=41. Hence d_A(u)<=a-41=44-q.
N_A(u) has no triangle and no I5, hence has order at most13 by R(3,5)=14. Combine the two bounds.
claims.improvement: Strengthens the universal interior cap13 at all a=50..53 without assuming connectivity or a small cross count.

claims.scope: Every ambient candidate in the setting. Write L=L(q), or max(1,L(q)) if connectivity is additionally assumed; D=min(13,44-q). Let m_i count A vertices of global excess i, t=m_0.
conclusion: Every row satisfies max(0,17+epsilon_u-D)<=r_u<=min(17,17+epsilon_u-L). In particular r_u=17 forces epsilon_u>=L; if L=4 this excludes size17 rows at excess0..3.
If t>0 some adjacent degree18 root u has overlap lambda_vu=d_A(u)<=min(D,floor((170-2q-sum_{i=1}^6 m_i max(L,i))/t)).
If E<=17 some adjacent degree18 root u has overlap at most min(D,floor((170-2q-L E)/(18-E))). This is a statement about one companion root, not an assertion that it shares q or E with v.
proof: The row identity and the degree bounds L<=d_A(u)<=D give the two row inequalities; combine with the recorded r_u<=17. The latter also implies d_A(u)>=epsilon_u.

The total interior degree is 170-2q. Each excess-i neighbor has interior degree at least max(L,i). Subtract their degree contribution; the average over the t degree18 neighbors bounds the interior degree of at least one such neighbor. Adjacent-root overlap is exactly that interior degree, and every vertex obeys the cap D.

For the simplified expression put z=sum_{i>0}m_i. Then z<=E<=17 and t=18-z>0. The previous average is at most (170-2q-L z)/(18-z). This expression is increasing in z because 170-2q-18L>=0 (also a necessary consequence of all 18 degrees being at least L). Replace z by E and take floors. No assumption is made that the chosen neighbor is itself a maximum-edge pivot.
claims.limits: These improve parameter-conditioned pair filters; the worst-case W<=10 overlap table need not improve. No occurrence of the listed profiles, selected-root equality, or complete d18 exclusion follows.

evidence_limits: Pure mathematical proof and trivial scalar validation only, no candidate graph search or catalogue processing.
No novelty review, certified nonexistence result, Lean proof, or change to executable pruning.
Older reviewed proofs remain unchanged; these claims are separately reviewable transfers.
